RETIRED 2026-08-31, when the client stopped shipping an un-themed "Classic" appearance. This was the themed twin of client-retransmission.png: the same Transmission fixture spec on the same device (TS.702) under a second filename, so the default (no-theme) pass and the --theme pass could each render the transmission grid without overwriting the other's image. The activity rail on its own, from CaptureActivityRail under --theme. The manual documents the rail as a surface in its own right and a 1920px window shot cannot show a 48px column legibly, so this is grabbed from the rail widget rather than cropped out of workbench-window.png. The fixture seeds three iconed pages (Overview/Alarms/Trends) so the middle band reads as a group rather than as one button, which is the whole point of the band; the capture asserts all three zones are present, so an image missing one fails rather than being published. Shows the admin session: the Nodes and Administration modes and the Users utility are hidden for everyone else. NOT YET A WINDOWS RENDER (re-rendered on macOS 2026-08-30, originally 2026-08-02): carries macOS fonts and metrics — re-render on Windows before publishing. The 2026-08-30 pass is a real UI change, not a re-render: the rail took VS Code's macOS activity-bar geometry (48px rail and 48px items against the previous 52/44, a 2px full-height active marker against 3px) and its glyphs dropped from 24px to 20px. The pages band was then replaced outright by a horizontal separator above the pages group: the band did not read at the native rail's density (measured 8/255 off the rail as a fill, 15 with rules) and the rule lands at 129 against a 30 rail. The web client keeps the band — see docs/client/ux/shell.md §2.1. The rail is 49px from 2026-08-30, not 48: it gained its own 1px right edge, without which it and the Explorer beside it were the same colour and ran together. Items are 48 wide but 40 tall from the same pass, following VS Code's glyph-to-item ratio rather than its pixel count, since our 20px SVG glyph puts more ink on screen than its 24px codicon. The glyphs were re-centred too — the active marker's left border had been reserved on one side only, putting every glyph 1px off axis. Kept out of current_generator_owned_subset (subset is auto-* only).

The preferences surface, from CaptureSettingsPanel. **The filename says `dialog` and the surface is no longer one.** `SettingsDialog` was retired on 2026-08-28 for `SettingsPanel`, a full-window overlay over the workbench (backlog 626), and the capture was retargeted at it in the same change — but the tracked PNG here is still the last render of the retired dialog, because a re-render has to happen on Windows and the manual pages that embed it still describe a dialog. Backlog 628 carries the three as one change: rename the capture and the file, rewrite scada-docs client/workbench.md in both languages, re-render on Windows. Until then this row is knowingly stale, and a diff against it means nothing. What the capture now asserts: the panel is built from the row catalogue joined to the Settings MenuModel, so it shows exactly what the shell publishes — the framework toggles, every module's MainMenuId::Settings contribution, and the Language / Style / Colour scheme choice rows — plus the three things that make it a surface rather than a dialog (the search field, the category table of contents, the scope tabs) and the `Open Displays Folder` action row, which is backlog 554's answer and which the dialog could not carry. A row offering the four appearances must still be present, because Colour scheme is how the operator picks one and it must not become unreachable. Replaces colour-scheme-menu.png, whose submenu no longer exists. This capture used to skip under --theme and publish `legacy`, because the operator who needed it was the one still on Classic; Classic is gone, so it renders under the theme like every other capture and the tracked PNG below is doubly stale — it shows both the retired dialog and the retired appearance. NOT YET A WINDOWS RENDER (re-rendered on macOS 2026-08-26, offscreen, hermetic HOME) — re-render on Windows before publishing. The Language combo reads Русский where the 2026-08-02 render read English; that is not a regression — the tracked file predates 3487975be (2026-08-15, 'qttranslations was in no manifest, so Qt chrome shipped English'), so it was captured with Qt's own catalogue absent and the combo fell back to the English source. Ruled out as leaked machine QSettings: that render was byte-identical with and without a hermetic HOME.

Graph window with a time cursor: the capture now places and selects one (GraphAxis::AddCursor + Graph::SelectCursor) so the themed legend's '@ cursor' column is populated - before that it rendered no cursor at all and every row read '-', despite the file's name. All three series now vary and the legend's Min/Max/Average differ per pane, once a history-service bug was fixed (a read whose upper bound was the current-only sentinel DateTime::Max spread its 48 points across ~285000 years, so all but the first fell outside the window and the series read flat). REWORKED 2026-08-16 (backlog 344): this row and limits-chart.png used to be two fixture rows differing only in `filename`, so both plotted the one shared `graph` object and rendered the same file byte for byte - each a superset of both subjects rather than an illustration of either. A screenshot row now names its own graph configuration in the fixture's `graphs` object, and this one plots the `cursor` variant: two panes (TIT.201 Реактивная мощность, TIT.208 Частота), neither carrying limit bands, with the time cursor the filename is about. The cursor is opt-in per configuration now, so it no longer appears in captures that are not about it. The tracked PNG is still the pre-change render - this tree renders on macOS and the gallery is regenerated from Windows - so expect this file to change at the next Windows regeneration (see the client-screenshots doc, and the standing list in backlog 310).

The Inspector as a chart selection fills it: the element card (title, node id, live value + quality pill, Measurements with the node's limit bands) over the SERIES section — the palette swatches with the plotted colour ringed, and the display flags. Until 2026-08-30 this captured a separate SeriesInspector widget that the Graph tab drew down the right edge of the chart; that panel was folded into the shell Inspector (backlog 673), because the two sat side by side naming the same series while trend.html draws one right-hand column. The capture still builds the fixture graph and routes its first series through a real SelectionModel, so the readout and the limits are live rather than filled by hand — they resolve because MakeGraphItemNodesResident makes the graphed node resident first, which is why no load_limits handler is wired. Reshell-theme and rides client_screenshot_check_themed, like its two Inspector siblings: the severity-coloured limit values return nothing under the legacy ramp. **The tracked bytes predate the fold** (290x480, the old widget); the spec is now 320x560 and the image is owed a regeneration from the Windows pipeline — see the backlog. Validation-only; not published to the manual.

Filled with an analog signal sitting above its Hi warning limit and carrying no output channel, so both the marked breach and the disabled-control explanation render. The panel paints the reshell's dark tokens whatever the host palette is, which is why this was `reshell-theme` from 2026-08-23: as `auto-view` it was rendered by the legacy no-theme pass onto a light window, and the tracked bytes (verified byte-identical to a fresh legacy render that day) showed the title, the update time and three of the four limit values as light grey on light grey - the card's data was present and unreadable. Its two siblings had already been moved for the same class of reason (inspector-event.png and series-inspector.png, both severity-coloured), so this is the third instance rather than a new rule. In the themed-ctest --only list. Published from a macOS render pending the Windows update-screenshots review; candidate for current_generator_owned_subset after that review.

Configuration workbench device-diagnostics inspector (DeviceDiagnostics): link-status hero (up/down/disabled), then the PROTOCOL LINK section and the device's own traffic/polling counters. Reshell-only chrome (backlog 5.0), captured under --theme against a fixture device (TS.103). Standalone like series-inspector; the capture wires the same load handler the shell wires and lets the panel fetch what it reads, rather than making the device resident on its behalf. Grew from 300x520 to 320x660 on 2026-08-23, when the fixture gained the Iec60870LinkType link TS.103 hangs under: until then no device in the gallery had a link, so ADR 0007's nine APCI rows, the section heading and the Reconnect action were rendered by no capture at all - and the tracked image still showed a Reconnect button the generator had stopped producing. The link is Running while the RTU is silent (t1 expired, two frames unacknowledged), which is the state the hero's `device is not responding` describes. Not yet embedded in a manual page.

The device Metrics sheet — what *Метрики* on a device's context menu opens (client.md, "Статусы устройств"), and the Qt half of the web's DeviceMetrics component. Rendered for the fixture's КП-01 (TS.103, an IEC 60870-5-104 RTU): the row labels are the DeviceType data-variable declarations (Связь, Включено, Принято/Отправлено сообщений и байт, Число синхронизаций времени, Число полных опросов) and each cell is an `=NodeId` formula the sheet resolves live. Not a window type of its own — DeviceMetricsModule builds a CusTable WindowDefinition from resolved NodeRefs, which do not exist when MakeScreenshotPage assembles the profile page, so the capture opens its own view. Not yet embedded in a manual page: it is half of what devices-status.png shows, and replacing that figure is still open (tasks.md 39, subtask 8). Booleans still render 0/1 where the hand-captured devices-status.png shows Да/Нет — a real formatting gap, filed separately. The byte counters no longer render in scientific notation: verified 2026-08-31 against a fresh themed render, which shows 4213904 / 1830221 as plain integers. Published 2026-08-15 as the Метрики half of `devices-status.png`. This was the last image opted out of the dark publish pass (publish_theme=legacy): it could not render themed at all, because MakeDeviceMetricsWindowDefinition baked Rgba{227,227,227} into the header cells as *window definition* data while the body cells fell back to white, so a themed render darkened only the frame and the scrollbars. Both halves are fixed — the baked header fill is gone and unstyled cells now fall through to the theme palette — so the sheet renders under any appearance. The tracked PNG predates that and is a Classic render.

Device log (Watch view) for КП-01: the filter bar over a seeded IEC 60870-5-104 session — decoded Dir/Type/Cause/IOA/Fmt/N(S)/N(R) columns, plus a t1 timeout and a link loss carrying their severity colours. Rendered from the fixture's `device_log` block, delivered as event notifications by the generator's fake monitored-item service; the `rows` guard is 12 (11 seeded lines plus the one `events` entry sourced on this device). Was an empty grid for months because nothing bound a device to the view and nothing seeded events. Not published yet: no manual page embeds it. Re-rendered 2026-08-01 with the aui alignment fix: table rows are vertically centred (the adapter returned the horizontal flag alone, which Qt reads as AlignTop). Published 2026-08-15 in place of `devices-traffic.png`, which showed this same view inside the whole main window; the chrome around it is `workbench-window.png`'s subject, not this page's. Re-rendered dark for the published subset.

Administration explorer pane (the left region of users-admin.html): the section list the rail's Administration mode opens. Standalone chrome like users-rbac, captured under --theme; the pane normally derives its rows from the shell's live command resolution (ControllerDelegate::ResolveViewCommand), which the headless generator has no shell for, so the capture supplies every candidate section - what an administrator holding Configure sees. Sections are the admin-gated views that already have an entry point; roles / password policy / audit log join the list as they are built. Not yet embedded in a manual page. The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. Embed it on the next Windows regeneration, set published:true and add it to current_generator_owned_subset.

The Roles view: every Role of Server.ServerCapabilities.RoleSet with the accounts it is granted to, read via the identity mapping rules (Part 18 4.4.3). Admin-gated (WIN_REQUIRES_ADMIN), read-only. THEME-GATED, so reshell-theme rather than auto-view: MakeRolesGridPanel() returns nullptr under the legacy theme (the whole user_access panel family does), so RolesView::Init builds no widget, OpenedView::Init throws 'Can't create widget', and the view never opens. Tagged auto-view until 2026-08-02, which made every default-pipeline run fail this capture - the admin gate was NOT the cause, the session holds Configure. To publish it, the panel factory must first drop its legacy gate (the publish subset admits auto-* only). KNOWN FIXTURE GAP: Members renders 'None' for every Role. The RoleSet and its Roles browse correctly - the capture shows both - but the identity-rule rows the fixture projects under them do not come back from the client browse, so no membership reaches the view. The read path itself is unit-tested against FakeNodeService (role_membership_unittest.cpp); it is the offline fixture's rule projection that is unproven. Fix that before publishing this image. The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. Embed it on the next Windows regeneration, set published:true and add it to current_generator_owned_subset. CAPTURED STANDALONE since 2026-08-08 (SaveRolesScreenshot / SaveUsersGridScreenshot in user_access_capture.cpp), not through the view path: the grid is built from the server's published role->permission map, which needs ReadRolePermissions, and the generator's ordinary session is anonymous - so the view-path capture rendered 'No data' over an empty grid. AuthenticatedAttributeService supplies the administrator identity for these captures only. The member/role columns were additionally empty until a client fix the same day (ReadRoleMemberships did not fetch the rule type's chain, so no identity mapping rule read back); the tracked PNG still predates both and will change on the next Windows regeneration.

The Password policy view: what the server publishes on the UserManagement object (OPC UA Part 18 5.2.2) - the length range, the required character classes, and the deployment's own wording of the rule, shown verbatim. Read-only; the policy is server configuration. THEME-GATED, so reshell-theme rather than auto-view: MakePasswordPolicyPanel() returns nullptr under the legacy theme, so the view builds no widget and never opens - same gate and same 2026-08-02 retag as roles.png. The fixture configures no policy, so the capture shows the unconstrained case (Any length, nothing required) - which is a REAL state and deliberately distinct from 'No data', the unreadable case that also suppresses every requirement row. The manual prose for this surface is written (scada-docs client/workbench.md + en/ mirror, #administration); the image is NOT embedded yet because the published set must come from the WINDOWS pipeline - a macOS render differs by font alone and would commit as churn. Embed it on the next Windows regeneration, set published:true and add it to current_generator_owned_subset.

The Audit log view: the event journal scoped to the AuditEventType subtree (see client/modules/events/audit_events.h). Admin-gated. The capture demonstrates the filter rather than asserting it - the fixture seeds 13 events of which 4 carry audit types, and only those 4 appear. Acknowledgement chrome is deliberately absent (no unacknowledged-only toggle, no Acknowledge-all footer): an audit entry records that something happened, and there is nothing to acknowledge. The refused call renders in the warning band, which is the row an operator is looking for. NOT published: the published set comes from the WINDOWS pipeline; embed on the next regeneration.

The users-admin RBAC inspector (right region of users-admin.html) for the fixture's Администратор. Rewritten 2026-08-01 onto the ROLE model: it lists the Roles the account holds and derives the permission breakdown from them through the same default role->permission map the server enforces with, replacing the coarse Administrator/Operator/Observer pill that read the retired AccessRights bitmask - a pill that would have kept asserting authority for an account whose Role had been revoked. Three states stay distinct: the Roles list, 'None' (holds no Role - real, and grants nothing), and 'No data' (the RoleSet could not be read, which also suppresses every permission row). The Roles list is real as of 2026-08-08: this capture shows Operator, ConfigureAdmin. It showed 'None' until then, which was a CLIENT bug rather than a fixture gap - ReadRoleMemberships resolved a rule's Criteria through the type's property declarations without fetching the type chain, so every rule read back empty against the real node model (regression test: ScreenshotGenerator.RolesEnumerateTheirMembers). SECOND FIXTURE FACT, easy to trip over: the panel now READS what each Role grants from the server (the RolePermissions attribute, Part 3 5.2.9) instead of carrying its own map, and that attribute requires ReadRolePermissions. The generator wires the real attribute service straight into the client, so the client's empty ServiceContext -- which a real server would have replaced with the session's identity -- reads as ANONYMOUS and the attribute is refused, collapsing the whole panel to 'No data'. AuthenticatedAttributeService supplies the administrator identity for this capture only; do not widen it to the generator's other services, which would change UserAccessLevel narrowing and with it every writability affordance.

Transmission-rules editor inspector (TransmissionRule): the right region of transmission-rules.html for a selected transmission item — source signal + type tag (TS/TI), destination endpoint + IOA, and protocol (Modbus / IEC 60870-5-104 / IEC 61850, from the item's type). Reshell-only chrome (backlog 5.2), captured under --theme against a fixture rule (TS.733 TX_Ua → Modbus IOA 2001). Standalone like users-rbac; the capture makes the rule + its type chain, source and parent endpoint resident so ShowRule resolves the source/endpoint and reads SourceAddress. Read-only in this capture (no shell write path); the mockup's Trigger/Transform/Status/counters are server-side driver concepts absent from the client node model. Not yet embedded in a manual page.

Bulk-create wizard preview (BulkCreate): the naming/addressing step of bulk-create.html — a {n}-token name + NodeId pattern, start/count/step + IOA start/step, and a live preview grid (# / Name / NodeId / IOA / Status) with a 'N new / M conflict' summary. Reshell-only chrome (backlog 5.4), standalone and node-service-free: the capture seeds a demo pattern (TS{n} current, 12 items from IOA 4001) and one existing NodeId (TS8), so row 8 flags as a red 'exists' conflict. Driven by the pure ExpandBulkCreate engine. The actual node creation rides the existing MultiCreateModel::Run (Session.addNodes). Not yet embedded in a manual page.

Theme-gated reshell chrome (backlog 5.0/4.2); the legacy view is a bare tree, so it is excluded from the no-theme managed check. Fixture devices KP-01 offline / KP-02 online / KP-03 disabled. Custom table (the CusTable window, SheetModel) — the free-form spreadsheet: literal labels beside '=<formula>' cells bound to live values, with a coloured title and header band. Untagged until 2026-08-01, so the managed-image gate skipped it, and the render was a blank grid: a sheet's content lives in its saved window as SheetCell/Column items, which no fixture spec could express. The spec now carries `cells` and `column_widths` (see screenshot_data.json), and the capture is guarded by a filled-cell count — a sheet's row and column counts do not move when its content vanishes, so only counting cells that rendered text can see it go empty. Column headers (A/B/C) and row numbers are deliberately absent: sheet_view.cpp shows them only in edit mode. A live cell renders its item's display format (Температура shows 42.3; Активная мощность has no format and shows 125). That exposed a third bug: a formula cell cached the text it formatted when the sheet opened, and nothing notifies when an item's format arrives, so `--only sheet.png` rendered raw values where a full run rendered formatted ones — and a real sheet opened before its nodes loaded stayed unformatted for the life of the window. Formula cells now format on read (SheetCell::GetDisplayText), and the two renders agree. Populating this capture found a teardown crash: ~SheetCell erases itself from SheetModel::blinking_cells_, which was declared after `cells_` and so destroyed before them — closing a sheet holding one blinking cell segfaulted in std::set::erase, reachable by any user whose custom table binds a cell to a live value. Fixed by declaration order, with a regression test in sheet_model_unittest.cpp. It also found the alignment bug this capture now demonstrates: per-cell alignment was parsed, stored and offered in the context menu but never reached the screen, because GridCell carried no alignment and the grid adapter handed Qt the aui enum raw — so every aui::Grid in the client rendered left-aligned whatever its columns asked for. Fixed in grid_model_adapter.cpp + GridCell, with tests in grid_model_adapter_unittest.cpp; summary.png and client-retransmission.png changed with it. macOS render pending a Windows re-render; validation-only.
